title: Applied anatomy: the kidney and ureter (stones and ureteric injury)

related.why: Pelvic anatomy: rectum and anal canal

brief.role: Core surgical trainee in the urology clinic
brief.scenario: Mr Gareth Llewellyn, 45, has severe right loin pain radiating to the groin and right testis, with microscopic haematuria. Low-dose non-contrast CT shows a 6 mm stone at the right vesicoureteric junction. Written findings: a view of the posterior abdominal wall with the peritoneum and bowel removed shows both kidneys on the posterior abdominal wall either side of the vertebral column. Each has an adrenal gland on its upper pole. At each hilum three structures enter, arranged from front to back. Behind each kidney lie the diaphragm above, and below it a longitudinal muscle beside the vertebral bodies and a flat muscle lateral to it.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the anatomy of the kidney and ureter, and relate it to his stone and to ureteric injury at surgery. The examiner will read out further findings as the station goes on.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Kidney, course of the ureter, three narrowings, referred pain, blood supply, then safety.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Saying ureteric pain is referred through S2–S4.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "The ureter runs down on psoas and crosses the pelvic brim at the common iliac bifurcation."

grid.label: Kidney
grid.fail: Places the kidney inside the peritoneum or cannot give the hilar order.
grid.pass: Retroperitoneal, roughly T12 to L3, right lower than left; hilum front to back: vein, artery, pelvis.
grid.high: Gives relations: right with liver, duodenum and hepatic flexure; left with spleen, pancreatic tail and splenic flexure; posteriorly diaphragm, psoas and quadratus lumborum.

grid.label: Course of the ureter
grid.fail: Cannot describe the course, or puts the ureter behind the iliac vessels.
grid.pass: Descends on psoas, crosses the pelvic brim in front of the common iliac bifurcation, runs down the side wall and enters the bladder obliquely.
grid.high: Gonadal vessels cross in front in the abdomen; the vas crosses above it in men; the uterine artery crosses above it beside the cervix.

grid.label: Narrowings
grid.pass: Pelviureteric junction, crossing of the iliac vessels at the pelvic brim, and the vesicoureteric junction, the narrowest.
grid.high: Links his distal 6 mm stone to NICE NG118: consider an alpha blocker for distal ureteric stones under 10 mm.

grid.label: Referred pain
grid.fail: Says ureteric pain is referred through S2–S4, or cannot explain loin to groin.
grid.pass: Visceral afferents run with sympathetic nerves to T11–L2, so pain moves from loin to groin as the stone descends.
grid.high: Adds genitofemoral and ilioinguinal territory: scrotum or labium and upper thigh, so testicular pain with a normal testis may be ureteric.

grid.label: Blood supply
grid.fail: Plans to strip the ureter clean during mobilisation.
grid.pass: Segmental supply from renal, gonadal, aortic, iliac and vesical branches: abdominal part from the medial side, pelvic part from the lateral side.
grid.high: Branches anastomose longitudinally in the adventitia, so preserve it and handle the ureter minimally.

grid.label: Ureteric injury at surgery
grid.fail: Cannot name operations where the ureter is at risk.
grid.pass: At risk in hysterectomy (under the uterine artery), sigmoid and rectal resection (pelvic brim, mesenteric pedicle) and aortic surgery.
grid.high: Identifies the ureter before dividing pedicles; if injured, recognises it on table and calls a urologist.

grid.label: Emergency safety
grid.fail: Treats fever with an obstructing stone with antibiotics alone.
grid.pass: Obstruction with infection: urgent decompression by nephrostomy or ureteric stent, plus antibiotics.
grid.high: Pain relief per NICE NG118: NSAID first, IV paracetamol if unsuitable, opioid only if both fail; no antispasmodics.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Describe the kidney from the written findings.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It's in the abdomen, inside the peritoneum. I'm not sure of the order at the hilum.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Describe the course of the ureter.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It goes down behind the iliac vessels into the bladder.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Why is his pain in the groin?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How would you protect the ureter when mobilising it?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Clean it right down so I can see it well.

fail.speaker: examiner

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: He's now febrile with the stone still there.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Start IV antibiotics and wait for it to pass.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Retroperitoneal, roughly T12 to L3, the right lower than the left. At the hilum from front to back: vein, artery, pelvis.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Describe the course of the ureter.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It descends on psoas, crosses the pelvic brim in front of the common iliac bifurcation, runs down the side wall and enters the bladder obliquely.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The pelviureteric junction, the pelvic brim where it crosses the iliac vessels, and the vesicoureteric junction, which is narrowest. His is there.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Visceral afferents travel with sympathetic nerves to T11 to L2, so the pain moves from loin to groin as the stone descends.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Segmental: renal, gonadal, aortic, iliac and vesical branches. The abdominal part is supplied from the medial side, the pelvic part from the lateral side.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: When is it at risk at surgery?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hysterectomy, under the uterine artery; sigmoid and rectal resection at the brim and mesenteric pedicle; and aortic surgery.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: An infected obstructed kidney needs urgent decompression, a nephrostomy or stent, as well as antibiotics.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: On the right: liver, duodenum and hepatic flexure. On the left: spleen, pancreatic tail and splenic flexure. Behind: diaphragm, psoas and quadratus lumborum.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The gonadal vessels in front in the abdomen. In men the vas crosses above it; in women the uterine artery crosses above it beside the cervix.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How would you manage this stone?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It's distal and under 10 mm, so NICE NG118 says consider an alpha blocker, if his pain is controlled and there's no infection.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: He also has pain in the right testis.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Genitofemoral and ilioinguinal territory, from the same segments. I'd still examine the testis, but pain with a normal testis may be ureteric.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Why does the blood supply matter?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The branches anastomose along the adventitia, so I'd preserve it and handle the ureter as little as possible.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How do you avoid injuring it?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Identify it before dividing any pedicle. If I injure it, I'd recognise it on table and call a urologist.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: NICE NG118: NSAID first, IV paracetamol if that's unsuitable, opioid only if both fail. No antispasmodics.

failures.move: Giving antibiotics alone for an infected obstructed kidney.
failures.consequence: Pus under pressure: risks sepsis and loss of the kidney.
Cannot explain loin to groin pain or testicular pain with a normal testis.
Devascularises it, risking stricture or leak.

failures.move: Dividing pedicles without seeing the ureter.
failures.consequence: Ureteric ligation or transection that may not be recognised.

recovery.line: Psoas, pelvic brim at the iliac bifurcation, side wall, bladder.

recovery.when: Asked about fever with a stone
recovery.line: An infected obstructed kidney is an emergency: decompress it.

knowledge.fact: Kidney: retroperitoneal, T12–L3; hilum front to back vein, artery, pelvis.
Ureter crosses the pelvic brim in front of the common iliac bifurcation; uterine artery and vas cross above it.
Narrowings: pelviureteric junction, pelvic brim, vesicoureteric junction.
Ureteric pain: afferents to T11–L2; loin to groin, scrotum or labium.
NICE NG118: NSAID first; consider alpha blocker for distal ureteric stones under 10 mm.
Obstruction with infection needs urgent decompression.

recall.think: Infected obstructed kidney; ureteric injury at surgery.
recall.say: "Ureteric pain is referred through T11 to L2."
do: Trace psoas, brim, side wall, bladder
recall.trap: S2–S4 referral; antibiotics alone for an obstructed infected kidney.
recall.finish: Alpha blocker or surgery; decompress if infected.

sources.name: Gray's Anatomy for Students (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)
sources.supports: Kidney position, relations and hilum; course, relations and narrowings of the ureter; segmental blood supply; visceral afferents from the ureter to T11–L2 and referred pain to the groin and genitalia

sources.name: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery (O'Connell, McCaskie, Sayers, eds)
sources.supports: Ureteric colic, infected obstructed kidney and urgent decompression; iatrogenic ureteric injury in pelvic and abdominal surgery

sources.name: NICE guideline NG118: Renal and ureteric stones: assessment and management
sources.supports: NSAID first line, IV paracetamol if NSAIDs contraindicated or ineffective, opioids only if both fail, no antispasmodics; urgent low-dose non-contrast CT; consider alpha blockers for distal ureteric stones under 10 mm

partner.opening: You have the written findings of the posterior abdominal wall. Describe the kidney.

reveals.finding: Read out: a narrow muscular tube leaves the right renal hilum and runs down to the bladder. Describe its course and what crosses it, and say where along it a stone is most likely to lodge.
Pain controlled on diclofenac. Temperature 36.8 °C. Creatinine normal.
Next day: temperature 38.9 °C, rigors; stone unchanged, hydronephrosis on ultrasound.

push.question: Where does the ureter cross the pelvic brim?
push.expect: In front of the common iliac bifurcation.

push.question: Where do stones lodge?
push.expect: Pelviureteric junction, pelvic brim, vesicoureteric junction.

push.question: Why does the pain go to the groin?
push.expect: Afferents to T11–L2; genitofemoral and ilioinguinal territory.

push.question: How would you protect its blood supply?
He is now febrile. What do you do?

curveballs.prompt: At hysterectomy, where is the ureter most at risk?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Beside the cervix, where the uterine artery crosses above it; identify it before clamping.

curveballs.prompt: Should he have hyoscine for the spasm?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No. NICE NG118 advises against antispasmodics; NSAID first.

curveballs.prompt: He has testicular pain. Could it be torsion?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Examine the testis; referred ureteric pain leaves a normal testis. If in doubt, treat as torsion.
